# Intake brief — Explosions should be explosions (image-based explosion VFX)

> **Source request (verbatim):** "The explosions right now are just multiple
> circles. They look OK but we can improve them a great deal. Make them actual
> explosion images that change shape as they shrink. Each should be a subtle
> variation on the red/orange explosion colour."

## Problem statement

Every destruction burst is still rendered as a cloud of small filled circles,
so explosions read as "a lot of dots" rather than as an explosion. Replace the
circle particles with image-based explosion shapes whose silhouette changes as
they shrink and fade, tinted from a red/orange fire palette with subtle
per-particle variation.

## Users

- **Player** — the primary user; perceives destruction feedback.
  - *As a player, when I destroy an enemy or lose my ship, I see a recognisable
    explosion (a hot core, ragged flame lobes, sparks) rather than a spray of
    dots, so combat impact feels real and satisfying.*
- **Developer / designer** — tunes the look without touching gameplay code.
  - *As a developer, I can adjust the fire palette, frame count, morph timing
    and particle counts through named exported constants in one shared module
    and verify the behaviour deterministically in unit tests.*
- **Agent / maintainer** — must be able to change the look once.
  - *As a maintainer, I know the game and every gym consume the same VFX code,
    so a look change cannot drift between the game and the gym scenes.*

## Decisions pending producer confirmation

These three questions materially change the implementation and are recorded as
**OPEN QUESTION** entries in the Appendix. The ACs below assume the
**recommended** option for each, so the brief is implementable as written if the
producer accepts all recommendations.

1. **Art source** — procedural runtime-generated explosion textures
   (**recommended**) vs. committed raster sprite sheets vs. Graphics-only
   morphing polygons.
2. **Colour policy** — all explosions move to a red/orange fire palette
   (**recommended**) vs. keep the current per-entity hue and add a hot
   red/orange core vs. red/orange for enemy deaths only.
3. **Coverage** — every `spawnExplosionParticles` call site (**recommended**:
   enemy/boss/player deaths, victory fireworks, wave-timeout penalty, gyms) vs.
   entity-death bursts only.

## Existing state

- All destruction VFX route through one shared module,
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` (`spawnExplosionParticles()`), used by
  `BaseEnemy`, `Boss`, `CombatCoreScene._spawnPlayerExplosion`,
  `playerDeathJuice`, `endOfRunJuice` (victory fireworks/defeat) and the gyms
  (via the shared combat core), so game↔gym parity already holds.
- A burst is a **single Phaser `Graphics`** animated by one tween; each frame
  redraws every live particle as `fillCircle(p.x, p.y, p.radius)` with a
  colour from `jitterColor(baseColor)` (HSL jitter ±`EXPLOSION_HUE_JITTER_DEG`
  = 20° around the exploding entity's palette colour). Particles fade
  (`1 - fadeStep·elapsed`) and shrink over `EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS` (400 ms).
- Three patterns exist (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`) mapped per entity in
  `EXPLOSION_PATTERNS_BY_TYPE`; counts scale with entity size (clamped 8–80).
- Determinism: all jitter is drawn from a seeded PRNG (`createRng(seed)`), and
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` pins geometry, colour bands, counts,
  jitter and the Phaser integration through a structural scene double.
- Live per-kind counts are exposed by `getExplosionVfxCounts()` /
  `resetExplosionVfxCounts()` and consumed by the action-intensity metric.
- The repo ships **no image assets** today: `public/` contains only audio
  (`public/audio/sfx/*.wav`); every other visual is drawn procedurally
  (Graphics / shapes). Audio assets are baked from ToneForge recipes by
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- Documentation of the current circle rendering lives in
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.1–§7.2 (particle-effects and
  explosion-patterns bullets) and `README.md` ("Explosion VFX (particle
  bursts)").

## Desired change

1. Replace circle particles with **explosion imagery**: a small set of
   explosion shapes (e.g. 4–6 frames per burst family) whose silhouette changes
   over the burst's life as the particle shrinks and fades, so the explosion
   visibly *evolves* (hot dense core → ragged flame lobes → thin embers)
   instead of uniformly shrinking dots.
2. Use a **red/orange fire palette** with subtle variation per particle
   (hue/lightness jitter inside a constrained warm band, plus a brighter
   white-hot core), rather than the current entity-hue tinting.
3. Keep the existing pattern system (`radial`, `ring`, `implosion`), counts,
   lifespan, seeded determinism, teardown/registry contract and per-kind
   counters intact — this is a rendering/feel change, not a gameplay change.
4. Apply the change through the single shared module so the game and every gym
   get it automatically (no divergent copies).

## Acceptance Criteria

> AC1–AC3 depend on the recommended decisions (procedural textures, red/orange
> palette, all call sites). If the producer chooses another option, the ACs are
> revised before implementation.

- [ ] **AC1 — Explosion imagery replaces circles.** `spawnExplosionParticles()`
  renders each particle as an explosion shape from a cached, shared texture/frame
  set (no per-frame `fillCircle` particle rendering); a burst visibly reads as a
  blast (core + lobes/embers), not as a cloud of circles.
- [ ] **AC2 — Shape changes as the particle shrinks.** Each particle's shape
  frame is a deterministic function of its normalised age, so the silhouette
  morphs through at least 3 distinct frames from spawn to expiry while the
  particle also scales/shrinks; the final state is a thin ember, not a dot.
- [ ] **AC3 — Red/orange fire palette with subtle variation.** All explosion
  colours derive from exported warm-palette constants; 100% of emitted particle
  colours fall inside the documented red/orange hue band with bounded
  saturation/lightness variance (asserted across every colour the module emits,
  including cores, for both death bursts and victory fireworks).
- [ ] **AC4 — Behaviour preserved.** Pattern assignment, size-scaled counts
  (8–80), `EXPLOSION_LIFESPAN_MS`, seeded reproducibility (same seed ⇒ identical
  frames/colours/positions), the `opts.registry` teardown contract, the
  `getExplosionVfxCounts()` increments/decrements, the `delay`/`depth`/`scale`
  options and the null-scene guard all behave exactly as before.
- [ ] **AC5 — Single shared implementation / parity.** The change lives only in
  the shared VFX module (+ its texture helper); the game and every gym use it
  with no duplicated rendering code, and the repo-wide duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and gym-parity docs
  assertions still pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Deterministic, headless-testable tests.** Unit tests cover frame
  selection/morph progression, colour-band invariants, determinism, teardown and
  counters without a real WebGL canvas (texture provider is injectable/stubbable
  and preserves the existing structural scene double), and an in-game/gym visual
  verification is documented (GymFodderEnemies death bursts, player death,
  victory fireworks).
- [ ] **AC7 — Performance budget.** Concurrency stays bounded: no per-particle
  texture generation, frame textures are generated once and reused, and no
  regression in particle counts or teardown (no leaked display objects after
  scene SHUTDOWN/restart).
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation updated.** GDD §7.1–§7.2 (particle effects,
  explosion-patterns/colour table), the README "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)"
  section and the module header/comments describe the image-based look, palette
  and frame/morph constants, replacing the "small filled circles",
  "Hues stay recognisably 'that ship'", and per-entity colour statements.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No new runtime dependency**; stay on Phaser primitives.
- **Zero-asset repo convention** (recommended option): generate the explosion
  textures at runtime from code, cached by key; do not commit binary art unless
  the producer chooses the sprite-sheet option.
- **GDD §7.1 style rule**: "Geometric, angular shapes … No organic forms".
  Literal photographic/smoke-puff explosion images would conflict; the
  recommended look is a stylised neon blast (angular/ragged polygon lobes) to
  stay within the established art language — the producer may override.
- **Gym↔game parity** (repo convention / AGENTS.md): one shared code path.
- **Determinism**: seeded PRNG only; no `Math.random()` in VFX.
- **Performance**: bursts can be dense (Boss layers 3 patterns, victory
  fireworks up to 30 staggered bursts); textured particles must not multiply
  draw calls per particle in a way that breaks the current action-intensity
  budget. Use shared textures + batched images, and keep the existing count
  clamps.
- **Scope discipline**: gameplay numbers (damage, counts, timing, SFX) are out
  of scope; extra ideas are recorded as linked work items, not folded in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — replace the Graphics circle renderer with a
  pre-generated/cached explosion frame texture provider and per-particle
  image/quad rendering whose frame is a function of normalised age; add the
  warm-palette constants + colour resolution; keep the pure geometry/PRNG,
  pattern, lifecycle, registry and counter contracts.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts` — extend/extend-and-rename the pure-state
  and Phaser-double tests for frames, morph progression, colour band,
  determinism, teardown and counters.
- `src/vfx/explosionTextures.ts` (new, predicted) — procedural frame generation
  (deterministic polygon/blob silhouettes per frame) plus the texture cache/
  keyed registry and a headless-safe seam.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — the warm fire palette constants (or keep them in the
  VFX module, following the module's existing constant-export convention).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.1–§7.2 particle-effects and explosion
  pattern/colour text.
- `README.md` — "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)" section.
- Call sites that need no code change but must be visually verified:
  `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`,
  `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` (victory fireworks).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ambiguity risk** — the colour request may mean "keep ship identity but make
  the blast feel fiery". If the producer picks the recommended full red/orange
  palette, per-entity identity (Scout green, Diver yellow, Phaser magenta,
  player cyan) is intentionally lost and the GDD tables must change; this is
  recorded as an explicit assumption rather than silently decided.
- **GDD style conflict risk** — "no organic forms" vs. explosion images; the
  recommended stylised-neon-blast silhouette keeps the language, but a producer
  preference for realistic puffs would require an art pipeline.
- **Performance risk** — replacing one Graphics with N images per burst could
  regress frame time in dense scenes (Boss + fireworks). Mitigation: shared
  cached textures, a bounded texture count, batched rendering, and a check of
  the action-intensity/perf capture before review.
- **Test harness risk** — texture generation needs a canvas; the recommended
  procedural option must expose an injectable provider so headless Vitest runs
  stay deterministic and do not need WebGL.
- **Scope-creep risk** — tempting extras (screen-shake per particle, heat
  distortion, sound layering, per-entity explosion image families) are recorded
  as linked follow-up items, not added here.
- **Assumption** — the operator's "each should be a subtle variation on the
  red/orange explosion colour" refers to per-particle colour variation inside a
  warm palette, not a single flat orange.

## Related work

- **Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths**
  (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V) — the parent feature that introduced the circle-based
  particle bursts this item replaces visually.
- **Explosion pattern emitters and combinator** (AH-0MTVID632005ACBF) —
  `radial`/`ring`/`implosion` geometry that must be preserved.
- **Explosion particle test suite** (AH-0MTVH6DQO0016CGJ) — the test-first
  contract this change must extend rather than break.
- **Entity-centred explosion colour jitter** (AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034) — the
  per-entity hue jitter explicitly superseded by the new warm palette.
- **Add randomness to explosion** (AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH) — seeded size/position
  jitter that must remain deterministic.
- **Parity: gym↔game verification + explosion registry** (AH-0MUZQGRQR0086NP6)
  — the per-kind counter and parity guards that this change must keep green.
- **Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory** (AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44) and
  **Explosions timed with the beat** (AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3) — other consumers of
  `spawnExplosionParticles` whose look/behaviour must stay coherent.
- Related docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.1–§7.2, `README.md`
  (Explosion VFX), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§8.5 gym surface),
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` (VFX counters).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V** – Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths (completed)
- **AH-0MTVID632005ACBF** – Explosion pattern emitters and combinator (completed)
- **AH-0MTVH6DQO0016CGJ** – Explosion particle test suite (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.1–§7.2 explosion VFX/particle docs
- `README.md` — "Explosion VFX (particle bursts)" section
- `CHANGELOG.md` — release history

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Answers are pending; this intake stopped at the producer-review gate. Each entry
is an **OPEN QUESTION** with the agent's recommended option. Update in place
(never duplicate) when answers arrive.

- **Q1 (art source).** How should the explosion imagery be produced?
  (a) Procedurally generated at runtime into cached Phaser textures — keeps the
  repo's zero-asset convention and determinism; (b) committed raster sprite
  sheets/atlases under `public/` — needs an art source and an asset pipeline;
  (c) Graphics-only morphing polygons — lightest, but not really "images".
  **Recommended:** (a) — the repo ships no image assets, all VFX are code-drawn,
  and this keeps the seeded/deterministic test contract and gym↔game parity
  intact.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q2 (colour policy).** Should explosions drop the per-entity hue (Scout green,
  Diver yellow, Tank orange, Phaser magenta, Swarm blue, Boss red, player cyan)
  in favour of a red/orange fire palette with subtle per-particle variation?
  (a) Yes, every explosion becomes red/orange variants; (b) keep the entity hue
  as the base but add a red/orange hot core; (c) red/orange for enemy-death
  bursts only, keep player cyan and multi-colour victory fireworks.
  **Recommended:** (a) — matches the operator's wording ("subtle variation on
  the red/orange explosion colour") and the "explosions should look like
  explosions" intent; note this intentionally supersedes AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q3 (coverage).** Which burst sites adopt the new look? (a) All
  `spawnExplosionParticles` call sites — enemy/boss/player deaths, victory
  fireworks, wave-timeout penalty and every gym; (b) entity-death explosions
  only; (c) entity + player death only.
  **Recommended:** (a) — one shared implementation keeps gym↔game parity and
  avoids two explosion looks in one frame.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
- **Q4 (implicit, answered by repo research).** Do gym scenes need separate
  wiring? — Answer (agent research): No; gyms reach the VFX through the shared
  combat core and `spawnExplosionParticles`, so the change propagates
  automatically. Evidence: `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule.
- **Q5 (implicit, answered by repo research).** Is there an existing image asset
  pipeline to reuse? — Answer (agent research): No; `public/` contains only
  baked audio and the menu's GitHub data-URI SVG. Evidence: `public/` tree,
  `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts`, `scripts/build-audio.sh`.

## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: with the dev JSONL sink moving to an in-memory per-run buffer (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), a page reload or crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail. Streaming telemetry batches to the dev server during the run — instead of one run-end upload — bounds that loss to at most one flushed batch (~64 records, ~1.3 s of play) and removes the page-reload regression that localStorage previously masked.

## Context

- Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3 (in-memory dev sink; this item is explicitly deferred there).
- Current flow: the JsonlTelemetrySink buffers records in memory, flushes batches of 64 to the sink, and the whole run is POSTed once at run end (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash before that POST loses the entire run's telemetry; a reload also loses the buffer entirely once it is no longer localStorage-backed.
- Dev only: the same reasoning applies to the production remote sink, which already streams batches via `HttpTelemetryTransport` (with retry/backoff), so production is not affected.

## Proposed design

- Send each flushed batch to the dev endpoint as it is produced (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) instead of (or in addition to) the run-end upload.
- The server (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) currently stores each upload as one complete `session-<stamp>.jsonl` and runs the automatic evaluation per upload; a per-batch POST would create many tiny recordings and repeated evaluations. The endpoint (or a new `part` protocol) must therefore either:
  - append JSONL records to the run's open session file keyed by a run id/seed, and evaluate once at run end, or
  - keep the run-end upload and add a lightweight "heartbeat/checkpoint" mechanism that only recovers the tail on demand.
- UX/offline: batches sent while the dev server is unreachable should stay in the memory buffer (or a bounded queue) and be retried at run end; at most one batch may be lost on a hard crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A mid-run crash/reload followed by a run-end state loses no more than one flushed batch (~64 records / ~1.3 s) of telemetry; the rest is recoverable from the dev server.
- AC2: The server session file for a run contains its records exactly once (no duplication from partial + final uploads), and the automatic evaluation still runs once per run.
- AC3: Dev CLI tooling (`record-session`, `capture-gameplay`, `verify-dev-telemetry`) continues to work unchanged in behaviour.
- AC4: Full project test suite passes.

## Status

Open decision item — parked until the in-memory sink (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) lands. Do not implement concurrently with that item in the same worktree.
data.title: Crash resilience: incremental telemetry upload so a mid-run reload loses at most one batch

# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`

## Clarifications & assumptions (added during implementation)

- **Centipede has no CSV-backed seed config.** `centipede` is a linked-chain archetype
  (`src/entities/Centipede.ts` + `src/scenes/core/centipedeChain.ts` / `centipedeFormation.ts`),
  a wave opt-in with no `enemy-configs.csv` row (see the gym editor docs in
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.5). Adding a CSV/seed row would make it
  appear as a tunable/saveable enemy and break the committed-CSV ↔ seed-key parity test,
  so the AC's "centipede seed config" is realised as the **explicit seed-default
  exclusion list** (`march`, `centipede`) in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, honoured by the
  config resolver: `loadEnemyConfig('centipede').wrapAware === false`.
  `march` is the only CSV-backed exclusion and carries an explicit `wrapAware=false` cell.
- **Red-before/green-after convention.** These are test-first tests for the implementation
  item (AH-0MVKXBQVT000B2WL), so every new test is wrapped in Vitest's `it.fails` (repo
  convention, e.g. `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts`, `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts`
  force-field block). The implementation item flips them back to `it`; a leftover
  `it.fails` fails the suite once the field lands.
- **Contract pinned for AH-0MVKXBQVT000B2WL:** `wrapAware` is in `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`;
  `coerceEnemyConfig` coerces `true/false/1/0` and defaults absent/blank cells to `true`;
  `serializeEnemyConfigs` emits the column and round-trips it; every seed except `march`
  is `true`; `loadEnemyConfig('centipede')` is `false`; the column is editable through the
  generic `applyCsvEdit` plumbing with no per-field admin.

# Implement: shared post-motion edge wrap

Implementation slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3). One shared post-motion step wraps wrap-aware enemies across the seam instead of clamping them to the arena.

## Goal

Wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position in the shared scene entity loop (game + gyms), gated on `wrapAware`, so the whole wrapped playfield is the arena for every archetype except the classic exclusions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single shared post-motion wrap step lives in `src/scenes/core/` and is called from the shared entity loop used by both `PlayScene` and the gym scenes — no per-scene or per-entity copy.
- Wrap-aware enemies (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) wrap across the opposite edge when their motion would carry them off-screen; velocity and heading are preserved (no reflection).
- `march` and `centipede` remain unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge, centipede weaves within bounds.
- Formation bases and formation-shaping logic are unchanged — wrapping is entity-level only (per parent risk note).
- Steering that seeks the player remains stable near the seam (no oscillation); the shared wrap does not fight a steering state machine.
- No archetype other than the documented exclusions keeps bounded/clamped motion; any extra exclusion discovered is recorded as a code comment plus a documented divergence.

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

# Intake brief — Full-suite runs dirty the main checkout ship-config.csv

> **Source request (verbatim):** "Full-suite test runs (observed with
> changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leave
> src/data/ship-config.csv modified in the MAIN checkout
> (thrustAcceleration/maxSpeed/frictionDeceleration/controlScheme changes),
> even though the suite runs from a worktree. A test exercising
> GymPlayer.saveShipConfig writes through the dev-server CSV plugin whose root
> resolves to the main checkout (likely via the symlinked node_modules / vite
> project root). This trips the implement dirty-tree gate on later sessions,
> requiring a git checkout restore; it can also silently clobber an operator's
> tuned ship config. … add a guard so suites never write the repo's tracked
> CSV."

## Headline

Full-suite test runs leak writes to the tracked `src/data/ship-config.csv` in the **main checkout** even when the suite runs from a worktree, breaking the implement dirty-tree gate and risking silent clobbering of an operator-tuned ship config. Fix the dev-server CSV plugin's root resolution and add a guard so suites never write a tracked repository CSV.

## Problem statement

Running the full test suite (observed during changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leaves `src/data/ship-config.csv` modified in the MAIN checkout — `thrustAcceleration`/`maxSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration`/`controlScheme` diverge from the committed values — despite the suite having run from a worktree. The only writer of the tracked CSVs is the dev-server CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`): its write handler resolves `resolve(root, 'src/data/ship-config.csv')` where `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274), and the config store's dev-mode save (`saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves`, gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV`, which is `true` under vitest) issues a **relative** `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (`src/core/configStore.ts` lines 397–405, 569–586). In vitest's happy-dom integration project (default `window.location` = `http://localhost:3000`, verified in the installed vitest source), happy-dom's fetch resolves relative URLs against that origin — so a real (un-mocked) save PUTs to `http://localhost:3000/api/csv/...`; whatever server answers there can write through a root that points at the main checkout. Worktrees symlink `node_modules` to the main checkout (confirmed on four live worktrees), which lets Vite's project-root/package-root inference escape to the main checkout. The worktree's own `csv-seed.test.ts` reads its CSVs via `__dirname`, so a leaked write to the *other* checkout is not caught by the seed tests in the active checkout. Consequences: the implement dirty-tree gate fails on later sessions (manual `git checkout` restore required), and an operator-tuned ship config can be silently clobbered; it likely also explains intermittent `csv-seed` / `<suite exited 1>` smoke failures (AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL, AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP, AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2).

## Users

- **Developers / AI agents running the suite** — "As a developer I want suite runs to never modify tracked config files in any checkout, so the implement dirty-tree gate stays green and I don't have to restore files manually."
- **Designers/operators tuning ship config** — "As a designer I want my tuned `ship-config.csv` to survive test runs, so my balance work isn't silently overwritten."
- **Test suite maintainers** — "As a test author I want tests to exercise save behaviour against isolated fixtures, so the suite is deterministic and hermetic."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No tracked-file writes from suites** — Running the audit-accepted full suite (`npm --silent test`: `unit` + `integration` projects) from a worktree leaves every tracked `src/data/*.csv` (`ship-config.csv`, `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`) unchanged in **both** the active worktree and the main checkout. Verified by an automated pre/post `git status --porcelain` of both checkouts that runs as part of the change's tests (a regression guard the suite itself asserts).
2. **Root isolation in the plugin** — The CSV plugin never resolves write targets to a checkout other than the active project root: the implicit `process.cwd()` default is replaced by an explicit, verified root (derived from the Vite-resolved root, or an explicit option), and any request whose resolved target escapes the active root is refused with no file I/O (HTTP error + logged reason). Existing explicit-root test fixtures keep working unchanged.
3. **Test-mode write guard in the store** — Under the vitest/test harness (`import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'` detected in `configStore.ts`), `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` must never write a tracked repository file: they either update the registry only (documented no-op wrt disk, preserving registry semantics used by tests) or route writes to an isolated temp fixture. A direct unit test covers each save function under test mode asserting no file on disk changes.
4. **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. Add a comment in the integration tests documenting the relative-fetch/bridge pattern and verifying the bridge is installed for every real save.
5. **Documentation and full suite** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (plugin root semantics, test-mode guard and store save behaviour) and any relevant wiki/docs entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and the existing seed/validation tests (`csv-seed.test.ts`, `configStore.*`, plugin tests, gym save tests) remain green.

## Constraints

- Dev-only behaviour is preserved: while `npm run dev` runs from the active checkout, gym Save/Save As must still persist through the plugin to the committed CSVs (read-write dev workflow, AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA). Production builds stay read-only (`apply: 'serve'`).
- Atomic-write semantics (temp file + rename) and the post-save registry re-read (`reReadRegistry`) must be preserved on the success path.
- Test isolation is a requirement, not an option: current unit/integration tests already pin temp fixtures via explicit `root`; the gap is the default path and the dev-mode relative fetch. Do not weaken existing fixture patterns.
- Worktree isolation rules apply: implementation happens in a worktree; the main checkout is never edited directly.
- UK English for prose/comments; Markdown for work-item and code-doc prose.

## Existing state

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — `configCsvPlugin(options)`: `const root = options.root ?? process.cwd();` (line 274); `handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath), …)` for ship/enemy/difficulty CSVs. Registered in `vite.config.ts` with no options (`configCsvPlugin()`, so default root = `process.cwd()` of the dev server / test process).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isDev()` = `import.meta.env.DEV === true` (line 97); `fetchCsv`/`putCsv` use relative `/api/csv/...` URLs (lines 397–405, 569–586); `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` (lines ~612–660) gate only on `isDev()`.
- Vitest config (`vitest.config.ts`) — `unit` (node) and `integration` (happy-dom, default origin `http://localhost:3000`) projects; `isolate: true`; the full suite is `unit` + `integration`.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` (lines 80, 121–133) and `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — real plugin behind an ephemeral HTTP server against a **temp** root with an explicit fetch bridge; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts` / `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — `vi.mock('../../core/configStore')` replacing `saveShipConfig` with an in-process registry seed; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — reads CSVs via `__dirname`, i.e. relative to the **active** checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it.
- Worktree layout — `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with `node_modules` symlinked to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed on four live worktrees: wl-AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40-*, wl-AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V-*, wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q-*, wl-AH-0MVNT27XR0080I3C-*).

## Desired change

1. Make the plugin's write root explicit and safe: derive it from the Vite server's resolved project root (with an explicit override option), and refuse any write whose target resolves outside the active root. This removes the unpredictable `process.cwd()` default.
2. Add a store-level test-mode guard so the vitest harness can never write tracked files (registry-only no-op or temp-fixture routing), closing the relative-fetch escape route at the source.
3. Harden regression coverage: a suite-run cleanliness assertion (pre/post `git status` on both checkouts) plus unit tests for the new root guard and the test-mode guard.
4. Document the safe patterns (explicit roots, fetch bridges, module mocks) alongside the plugin and store modules.

## Key Files

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — replace the `process.cwd()` default root with an explicit/Vite-resolved root that is verified against the active checkout; add the escape-refusal guard; update `ConfigCsvPluginOptions` docs.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — tests for default-root behaviour (must not write outside active root) and the escape-refusal guard.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — add test-mode detection to `isDev()`/save guards; document relative-fetch + bridge pattern.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` / `configStore.integration.test.ts` — tests for test-mode save no-op/temp routing; fixture pattern comments.
- `vite.config.ts` — pass an explicit root derived from `server.config.root` if the plugin cannot self-derive it.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — optionally extend the seed check to also assert a clean worktree/main-checkout diff (the suite-run cleanliness guard may live here or in a new small test).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` (only if behaviour changes; otherwise untouched) — `_onSave` consumes `saveShipConfig`'s `ok/reason`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole": where the leak was first observed (`discovered-from`).
- **AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL** — "[test-failure] csv-seed.test.ts / configStore.integration.test.ts — ship-config.csv diverges from DEFAULT_CONFIG": the smoke symptom of a leaked write (`thrustAcceleration 390` vs `300`).
- **AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT** — "enemy-configs.csv working-tree change removes header and trailing newline (fails csv-seed tests)": sibling symptom on the enemy CSV.
- **AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP**, **AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2** — "[test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test": possibly same intermittent root cause.
- **AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA** (config-store epic), **AH-0MUE2MHRC0090AXP** (CSV plugin), **AH-0MUE2MIK9001TK88** (integration tests) — origin of the dev write-back design being hardened here.
- **AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V** — "Ship config controlScheme does not survive game server restart": dev-server persistence semantics for ship config.
- **AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4** — "Gym config save strips the CSV comment header block": another save-path quirk.
- **AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM** (open) — "Dev-mode write-back: gym Save to repo persists bot tuning": the same "dev writes to tracked repo data" family; keep separate.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-broad guard breaks the legit dev save flow** — mitigation: scope the refusal to (a) targets outside the active root and (b) test-mode; the dev-mode save path from the active checkout must keep working (AC2 keeps explicit-root fixtures valid).
- **Stray server on the happy-dom origin (localhost:3000) still receives writes if only the plugin changes** — the store-level test-mode guard (AC3) is the belt-and-braces fix; do not rely on the plugin alone.
- **Root-cause mechanism partially inferred** — the exact process that answers the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run was not reproduced deterministically in this intake; the implementer must reproduce and confirm before finalising the guard wording (record the reproduction in the work item). Non-blocking for the fix: ACs are observable-outcome based.
- **Scope creep** — protecting against an operator's accidental save overwriting a tuned config in the *browser/UI* (e.g. a confirmation prompt) is a separate UX concern; record it as a separate item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption** — `npm --silent test` remains the audit-accepted full suite; suite runs from implement worktrees use symlinked node_modules; vitest happy-dom default origin is `http://localhost:3000` and happy-dom resolves relative fetches against it (verified in installed `vitest`/`happy-dom` sources at intake time).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed context (title + description of AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) already contained the observed symptom, the primary hypothesis (root resolution via symlinked node_modules / vite project root), and the suggested fix directions. Research performed during intake:

- **Q (self): "Which code path is the only writer of the tracked CSVs?"** — Answer (Map): `configCsvPlugin.handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath))` in `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`; `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274). Source: code inspection of `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, `vite.config.ts` (plugin registered without options).
- **Q (self): "How does a suite-run write escape the temp-fixture pattern?"** — Answer (Map): all plugin instantiations in tests pass explicit temp roots (`configCsvPlugin.test.ts` line 100/447, `configStore.integration.test.ts` line 80) and GymPlayer tests mock the store — so the leak is not from these; the store's dev-mode save issues a relative `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (configStore.ts lines 397–405, 569–586) gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV` (true under vitest). In the happy-dom integration project, happy-dom's `Fetch` resolves the relative URL against `window.location.href` (verified in `node_modules/happy-dom/lib/fetch/Fetch.js`), whose vitest default is `http://localhost:3000` (verified in `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DC7d2Pf8.js` line 343). A real server on that origin with a root at the main checkout receives the PUT.
- **Q (self): "Why does the worktree's root resolve to the main checkout?"** — Answer (Map): worktree `node_modules` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed via `ls -la` on four live worktrees), so Vite's package-root/workspace-root detection and any module-relative path resolution can escape to the main checkout. Likely, not yet reproduced end-to-end (recorded in Risks).
- **Q (self): "Why doesn't the active checkout's csv-seed test catch the leak?"** — Answer (Map): `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` reads CSVs via `resolve(__dirname, …)`, i.e. the active checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it. Source: code inspection.
- **Q (self): "Are there existing related items?"** — Answer (Map): yes — AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL (ship-config smoke failure), AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT (enemy-config analogue), AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP / AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2 (generic suite-exit-1), AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V, AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4, AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM. Source: `wl search` during intake step 2.
- **Open question for the implementer (not a producer blocker):** reproduce the exact answering server/process on the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run and record it; the ACs are outcome-verifiable regardless.

# Limit the number of power-up slots

**Headline:** Cap the run's permanent loadout at six slots shared across power-ups *and* weapons; the first six distinct kinds taken as permanent rewards define the run, and once all six slots are full only those kinds (plus flagged always-available entries such as Extra Life and Mystery UFO) may spawn or be offered as a new permanent pick. Field pickups never consume a slot.

## Original request (verbatim)

> Currently the player can collect any number of powerups. This makes them way too powerful in late game. Limit the number of power-ups that can be collected to 6. The first 6 collected permanently (i.e. from the hull-full) become the only powerups the player can collect in that game. Once the 6 slots are full with permanent items no other powerup kind will spawn (a life powerup is an exception, there may be other exceptions later in the development cycles, so availability when full should become a flag on the powerup database entry). Until all 6 slots are full powerups will spawn as they do now.

> **Terminology:** the item text says "hull-full"; the shipped feature is the **hold-full choice** (`MineralChoiceScene`, driven by the mineral hold — GDD §4.5). This brief treats "hull-full" as "hold-full", i.e. a **permanent reward** grant. "Collected permanently" means a hold-full (or mini-boss reward) grant, never a field pickup.

## Problem statement

Players can currently collect every power-up and weapon kind in the catalogue, and every hold-full (permanent) reward can add a brand-new kind with no upper bound. By the late game a player therefore owns every permanent effect at once, which makes the ship far too powerful and flattens the difficulty curve. The run needs a bounded loadout: **six permanent slots shared across power-up and weapon kinds**. The first six distinct kinds the player takes as permanent rewards fill the slots; once all six are full, no other kind spawns or is offered as a new permanent pick, except kinds explicitly flagged as available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO today). Until the slots are full, spawning is unchanged.

## Users

- **Player (arcade run)** — wants a strong but bounded loadout, so late-game runs stay challenging and each run has a recognisable build identity; a drop on screen must still be worth catching.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the cap data-driven, with per-entry exemptions (Extra Life, Mystery UFO today; more later) needing no code change.
- **Agent / developer** — needs one shared implementation so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, once I have taken six permanent rewards my build is fixed for the rest of the run, so my late-game ship is strong but no longer invincible.
- As a player with six full slots, the only drops I see are the six kinds I chose (plus Extra Life and Mystery UFO), so every pickup improves something I own.
- As a designer, I can mark a catalogue entry as available-when-full, so a future exception is a data change, not a code change.
- As an operator, I can observe the identical slot rule in the gyms as in the shipped game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cap and shared accounting** — A single named, exported cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`) governs permanent ownership; occupied slots equal the count of **distinct drop kinds currently held** — power-up ids with a permanent level ≥ 1 (`PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` / `permanentGrants()`) **or** an active temporary (field-pickup) stack (`PowerUpLevelStore.getTempStacks()`), plus weapon drop ids with a permanent level ≥ 1 (`Player.getWeaponLevels()`) **or** an active temporary weapon stack (`Player.getTempWeaponStacks()`), i.e. one shared pool of six (producer answers 2026-10-27: Q4 = a). A slot is released when the temporary window expires (`clearTemporary` / `tickWeaponTimers`). Entries flagged `availableWhenSlotsFull` never occupy a slot (Q7 = a). The permanent cannon and the `reset` utility are never counted (they cannot be permanently granted). A unit test proves the accounting: six distinct held grants fill the pool, a repeat grant of an owned kind levels it up without consuming a new slot, a temporary stack of a new kind consumes one, and the slot frees again when the temporary window expires. Exempt entries and `reset` never occupy a slot.2. **Spawn gating at full slots** — When all six slots (permanent **or** temporary — the union) are filled, the drop-selection path (game and gyms, one shared implementation) draws only from the six held kinds plus every catalogue id flagged available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO are flagged by default) and the slot-exempt `reset` utility; every other power-up *and weapon* id is never drawn. Verified by a seeded/injected-rng unit test on the selection helper plus a `PlayScene` integration test that fills the slots and asserts a large sample of draws contains only held/exempt ids.3. **No behaviour change below the cap** — While fewer than six slots are filled, drop selection covers the full catalogue exactly as today: a regression test with a fixed rng seed produces the identical draw sequence before and after the change (power-ups and weapons alike).
4. **Choice gating at full slots** — Once the slots are full, a hold-full offer (and the mini-boss reward, which reuses the same option builder) offers **only items currently in the slots**: level-ups of permanently-owned kinds, base picks for kinds held only temporarily (taking one makes it permanent — it already occupies its slot), plus available-when-full entries (which never occupy a slot). A base entry that is neither held nor exempt is never offered, so a seventh kind can never be taken. Verified by choice-pool tests at 6 filled slots covering both power-up and weapon offers (producer answer 2026-10-27: Q6 = a, with the Q4 note: at full slots only offer items currently in the slots).5. **Data-driven exemption** — The exemption is a flag on the power-up catalogue entry (`availableWhenSlotsFull`, default `false`), not an `id === '…'` special case; Extra Life **and** Mystery UFO set it. A test asserts both are exempt, that every other catalogue entry defaults to non-exempt, and that a newly added entry is non-exempt unless it opts in. (No weapon exemption exists today; the flag stays power-up-only until a weapon needs one.)
6. **Parity and run scope** — The rule lives once in shared core code consumed by `PlayScene` and the formation gyms (guard: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / parity tests); slot state is run-scoped and resets on run restart (`PowerUpLevelStore.reset()` / `Player.resetWeaponLevels()`), and a temporary window's expiry also releases its slot. A parity/integration test proves the gym path and the game path consume the same gate.7. **Documentation and suite** — The GDD (§4.4 catalogue table and §4.5 hold-full choice) and `docs/BALANCING.md` document the shared six-slot cap and the exemption flag; the full project test suite passes with the change.

8. **Blocked collection at the cap with a distinct cue** — A drop whose kind is neither held, nor available-when-full, nor the slot-exempt `reset` utility is **not collectable** while the pool is full: on overlap it is not collected (no effect, no pickup cue, not removed), stays on the field, and plays a distinct **not-collectable SFX** — once per drop while it remains blocked — so the player can tell why the pickup failed (producer answer 2026-10-27: Q5 = b). When a slot frees (a temporary window expires) the same drop becomes collectable again. A test drives the shared collection seam at full slots and asserts: blocked drop kept, cue played exactly once, no effect/absorb applied; owned and exempt drops still collected; `reset` still collected; and the blocked drop is collectable after a slot frees.
## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1):** the rule must be implemented once in shared code (`src/powerups/*`, `src/scenes/core/*`) and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms. A gym may only diverge for a documented, disabled-feature reason — none is expected here.
- **Single counter, derived from existing stores:** no new slot counter. Slot occupancy is derived from the two permanent-grant stores (`PowerUpLevelStore`, `Player._permanentWeaponGrants`), so existing level semantics stay the only source of truth.
- **Existing level semantics unchanged:** a repeat grant of an already-owned kind still levels it up (field pickup = temporary level, permanent reward = permanent level).
- **Determinism:** selection must stay injectable-rng deterministic; no wall-clock or `Math.random()` reads inside the new pure helpers.
- **No catalogue removals and no weight retuning:** the cap gates which ids may be drawn, not relative weights. `GameRules.powerUpWeights` / `weaponWeights` keep their meaning for the ids that remain eligible.
- **No individual rebalancing:** the six-slot cap is the balance change; per-item power tuning is out of scope.

## Existing state

- **"Power-up database":** `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpEntry` / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (16 power-ups); `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` (power-ups) and `WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS` (weapon drops) in `src/core/rules.ts`; `WEAPON_DROP_IDS`/`CHOICE_POOL` list weapon drops alongside.
- **Permanent ownership (power-ups):** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)`, `permanentGrants(id)`, `getLevels()` (permanent kinds only) and `getEffectiveLevel`/`getTempStacks` for temporary pickups.
- **Permanent ownership (weapons):** `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon(id, permanent)`, `getPermanentWeaponLevel(id)`, `getWeaponLevels()` (permanent kinds only), `getTempWeaponStacks`; `resetWeaponLevels()` on run restart. The cannon can never be permanently granted (`isTimedWeapon` guard) and `reset` is not a `WeaponId`.
- **Game spawn path:** `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the level-resolved drop chance, then spawns `this.dropSpawner.next()`. The spawner is built once by `buildDefaultDropSpawner()` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`) as a `WeightedRandomSpawner<DropId>` over `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS + WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, with weights from `src/core/rules.ts`. A small asteroid also rolls an additive deterministic `extra_life` drop.
- **Gym spawn paths:** `GymFormationScene._spawnPowerUpDrop()` (`powerUpSpawner`), `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymWeapons`, `GymLevel` — deterministic round-robin spawners.
- **Hold-full choice:** `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `CHOICE_POOL`, `buildChoiceCandidates()`, `drawWeightedWithoutReplacement()`, `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT`; `chooseOptions()` is consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym, and the mini-boss reward reuses `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions()` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`).
- **Effects application:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect()` routes a collection to the power-up store's temporary stack or permanent grant; `Player.equipWeapon(…, permanent)` records weapon grants. No cap on distinct kinds exists today.
- **Docs of record:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (catalogue/table) and §4.5 (hold-full choice), `docs/BALANCING.md` (drop/choice balance), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (parity convention), `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Desired change

- Add `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` and an `availableWhenSlotsFull` flag on `PowerUpEntry` (Extra Life `true`, Mystery UFO `true`).
- Add a pure shared helper module (e.g. `src/powerups/slots.ts`) that, given the permanently-owned power-up ids, the permanently-owned weapon drop ids and the catalogues, answers: slots used, slots free, and whether a drop id may be drawn/offered. It owns the shared-pool and exemption rules — no `id === '…'` branches anywhere else.
- Apply that helper at the two decision points, both shared with the gyms:
  1. **drop selection** — the weighted draw excludes non-owned, non-exempt ids once the pool is full, for power-ups and weapons alike;
  2. **choice candidate construction** — `buildChoiceCandidates` excludes base entries that would create a seventh permanent kind once the pool is full, while owned level-up offers, exempt entries and the remaining candidates survive.
- Keep the below-cap path byte-for-byte equivalent in distribution (eligible set unchanged, weights unchanged).
- Cover with unit tests (helper + spawner + choice), integration tests (`PlayScene`), gym parity coverage, and documentation updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `availableWhenSlotsFull?: boolean` to `PowerUpEntry`; set `true` on `extra_life` and `mystery_ufo`; document default `false`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` (mirroring existing `POWER_UP_*` constants).
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` *(new)* + `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` — pure shared-pool accounting and eligibility (power-ups + weapon drops, exemptions included).
- `src/powerups/spawner.ts` — let a draw consult an eligibility predicate (or accept an eligible-id set) without weakening the all-zero-weight fallback.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — a shared `drawNextDrop(spawner, slotState)` seam (built on `buildDefaultDropSpawner`) so every scene draws through one filtered path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the run's permanently-owned power-up and weapon ids into the drop draw (keep the asteroid `extra_life` path untouched).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — gate brand-new non-exempt kinds out of `buildChoiceCandidates` at the cap (owned level-ups and exempt entries remain).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` / `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` / `src/entities/Player.ts` — expose the owned-permanent-kind view consumed by the two gates (no new counter).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — consume the same filtered draw path (no divergent copy).
- Tests: `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` (new), `src/powerups/spawner.test.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (parity guard).
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 catalogue table + §4.5 choice), `docs/BALANCING.md`, `README.md` if it states power-up/weapon rules.

## Related work

- AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P — *As the levels progress increase the number of enemies and decrease the number of power ups* (level-resolved drop chance; the supply-side counterpart of this demand-side cap).
- AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X — *Add level-scaling module and tunable rules* (where `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1/Max` live; candidate home for a tunable cap).
- AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8 — *Smart Bomb is too powerful* (precedent for a single-item dominance fix; this item fixes dominance by accumulation instead).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 / AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR — power-up level curves and the `GymPowerUpLeveling` parity gym (the permanent-grant model this cap counts).
- AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP — *P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon* (established that spawn pool and choice pool are catalogue-derived; the cap must not break that invariant).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention + duplicate-body guard.
- AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON — shared level-up option builder used by hold-full choice and mini-boss reward (the choice gate must be applied at the shared builder seam, not duplicated).
- AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX — *Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support* (the `ChoiceStrategy` seam the choice gate extends).
- AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV — *Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling* (permanent weapon-grant semantics; weapons now share this item's slot pool).

## Risks and assumptions

- **All-zero-weight fallback:** `WeightedRandomSpawner` falls back to the first entry when every weight is zero, so exclusion must not be implemented by zeroing weights — it must be an eligibility filter applied before/while sampling.
- **Empty eligible set:** if all six owned kinds are currently unofferable and no exemption applies, the eligible set must never be empty; the draw must degrade to exempt/weapon entries rather than crash or always return one id.
- **Shared-pool starvation (design consequence):** because weapons share the six slots, a weapon-heavy build can consume the pool before any power-up reward is taken. This is the producer's chosen semantics (Q1 answer (c)); the docs must state it so it is not later mistaken for a bug. Balance evidence may need re-recording (out of scope).
- **Weapons granted by other permanent paths:** mini-boss unlocks/upgrades that set a permanent weapon level ≥ 1 also occupy a slot (derived from the same store); a document + test should pin that behaviour so the pool cannot be over-filled silently.
- **Test churn:** `src/core/rules.test.ts` and `src/powerups/choice.test.ts` assert the catalogue-complete pool; those assertions need an explicit "below cap" context.
- **Bot/balance evaluation drift:** `src/ai/eval/*` simulates campaigns and will see a different late-game loadout; re-recording bot evidence is *not* in scope unless a gate fails (record as a linked follow-up if needed).
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD slot readout (`N/6`), persisting slots in checkpoints/saved runs, capping the mini-boss weapon unlock pool separately, and rebalancing individual power-up/weapon strength are out of scope; each becomes a linked work item rather than extra scope here.
- **Assumption (A1, resolved by Q1 answer (c)):** one shared pool of six across power-up and weapon kinds; field pickups excluded.
- **Assumption (A3):** no new player-facing HUD/UX surface is required by this item (producer did not request one; if wanted, it becomes an explicit AC or a linked item).
- **Assumption (A4):** the cap is a named code constant (default 6), not a persisted `GameRules` setting.
- **Assumption (A5):** the cap applies in the gyms as well as the game (parity); no gym is exempted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — What consumes a slot?** *Answer (producer):* **"c, field pickups are excluded"** — one shared pool of six across power-up *and* weapon kinds; temporary field-pickup stacks never consume a slot. **Resolved:** slots = distinct permanently-owned drop kinds (power-up permanent grants + weapon permanent levels), derived from the existing stores; no new counter. Source: interactive producer reply on AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF.
- **Q2 — Does the hold-full choice also stop offering new kinds at the cap?** *Answer (producer):* **"a"** — yes, the choice is gated too: at six filled slots it offers level-ups of owned items and available-when-full entries only, never a new non-exempt kind (mini-boss reward inherits the same gate through the shared option builder). **Resolved.** Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Q3 — Exemption flag and drops already on screen?** *Answer (producer):* **"a (Mystery UFO can also have the flag true)"** — the flag is `availableWhenSlotsFull` on the power-up catalogue entry (default `false`), set for **Extra Life and Mystery UFO**; drops of non-owned kinds already on screen when the sixth slot fills remain collectible for their temporary effect and simply stop spawning. **Resolved.** Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Assumption A3 (recorded, not contradicted):** no new HUD slot readout is required — if the producer wants an `N/6` indicator it becomes an explicit AC or a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A4 (recorded, not contradicted):** the cap ships as a named constant rather than a persisted `GameRules` field.
- **Assumption A5 (recorded, not contradicted):** gyms obey the same cap (parity).
- **Q4–Q7 (answered 2026-10-27 by producer, see blocking comment AH-C0MVRC08UJ009D0CM):** Q4(a) temporary pickups occupy a slot while held and free it on expiry, and a hold-full at full slots offers only items currently in the slots; Q5(b) block collection of a non-owned non-exempt drop at the cap with a distinct not-collectable SFX; Q6(a) the choice gate follows the union; Q7(a) exempt entries never occupy a slot.
- **Research note:** duplicate-work check performed (`wl search` on "powerup slots limit", "powerup cap", "power-up limit", "spawn pool", "hold-full choice pool", "too powerful", "power creep") — no item (open or completed) implements a permanent loadout cap, so this item is not a duplicate. Closest completed work is the level-scaled power-up *supply* reduction (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and the Smart Bomb power reduction (AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8); both are related, neither covers loadout breadth.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** – Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed)
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** – Make weapons both cumalative and time out (completed)
- **AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08** – Remove the Power Pellet power-up from the game (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvq006v9hr, 0mv8gpgbl009m0d8, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, 0mvl9p2sf009qfon (+507 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvq006v9hr, 0mv8gpgbl009m0d8, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, 0mvl9p2sf009qfon (+504 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, accept, accounting, add (+433 more)

## Plan: decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-25)

Effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium); the plan-approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (approval is requested only for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk), so no approval pause was needed. The brief's own Appendix already carried producer answers Q1–Q3, so no new questions were required.

**Phasing (vertical slices, test-first).** Every phase is a test + implementation pair so each slice is reviewable end-to-end; the docs phase closes the item. Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated against what actually shipped.

| # | Work item | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Test the six-slot accounting and exemption flag (AH-0MVNT2SD300874CP) | task | — |
| 2 | Shared six-slot helper, cap constant and exemption flag (AH-0MVNT2TEK001BNQ4) | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Test drop gating at full slots and below-cap parity (AH-0MVNT2XHB000YR2Z) | task | 2 |
| 4 | Gate the shared drop draw on the six-slot pool (AH-0MVNT2YGD003N8NR) | feature | 3 |
| 5 | Test hold-full choice gating at full slots (AH-0MVNT2Z89005OPKJ) | task | 2 |
| 6 | Gate choice candidates at full slots (AH-0MVNT2ZXK009Z5VU) | feature | 5 |
| 7 | Prove gym↔game parity and run-scoped slot state (AH-0MVNT30OT0074NNM) | task | 4, 6 |
| 8 | Document the six-slot cap and exemption flag (AH-0MVNT31C50065EE0) | docs | 4, 6 |

**Items 3–4 and 5–6 are independent branches** (drop draw vs choice pool) after item 2, so they may be implemented in either order; item 7 and item 8 need both.

**Acceptance-criteria coverage** (manual traceability check — the parent ACs are a numbered list, which the automated `tree_coverage` extractor does not parse, so coverage was verified directly; Jaccard scores of the best-matching child AC: AC1 0.84 (item 1), AC2 0.97 (item 4), AC3 0.97 (item 3), AC4 0.98 (items 5/6), AC5 0.65 (item 1), AC6 0.98 (item 7), AC7 0.96 (item 8)):

- AC1 (cap and shared accounting) → items 1, 2
- AC2 (spawn gating at full slots) → items 3, 4, 7
- AC3 (no behaviour change below the cap) → items 3, 4
- AC4 (choice gating at full slots) → items 5, 6
- AC5 (data-driven exemption flag) → items 1, 2
- AC6 (parity and run scope) → items 4, 7
- AC7 (documentation and suite) → item 8

No catalogue removal, no weight retuning and no per-item rebalancing are planned — the cap gates eligibility only, as the constraints require.

## Change of plan — 2026-10-25 producer audit (authoritative, supersedes parts of AC1–AC7)

The producer rejected the shipped implementation with this audit verdict (recorded
in the audit store, author `rgardler`, audited 2026-10-25T22:54:56Z):

> Rejected by manual review. Change of plan the slots should be limited to 6 slots
> for both permanent and temporary (field) pickups.

That verdict supersedes the earlier Q1 answer (c) ("field pickups excluded") and
the AC text that says field pickups never consume a slot. It is also **not** what
shipped in v0.1.15: `src/powerups/slots.ts` derives occupancy from the permanent
grants only, and the GDD §4.4 / `docs/BALANCING.md` say so explicitly. The delta
therefore has to be re-planned as a new increment on top of the eight closed
children (which stay closed).

### What the change touches

- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — occupancy (`resolveSlotState`), eligibility
  (`isWithinSlotPool` / `eligibleDropIds`) and the "full" definition.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — the candidate gate at full slots.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` / `PlayScene.ts` + the gym
  scenes — the callers that resolve the slot state.
- Tests that pin the current semantics (`src/powerups/slots.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/slots.weaponLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts`) and the
  docs assertions (`src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4/§4.5 and `docs/BALANCING.md`.

Temporary state is already exposed per kind (`PowerUpLevelStore.getTempStacks(id)` /
`getEffectiveLevel(id)`, `Player.getTempWeaponStacks(id)` / `getWeaponLevel(id)`), so
a temporary-aware occupancy can still be **derived** (no new counter) for option (a)
of Q4 below.

### Resolved — producer answers 2026-10-27 (all four answered; recorded in the
blocking comment AH-C0MVRC08UJ009D0CM)

- **Q4 → (a)** — a kind occupies a slot while held permanently **or** temporarily;
  the slot frees when the field-pickup window expires. Occupancy stays derived from
  the existing stores. With the answer came an explicit note: **if a hold-full is
  offered while all slots are full then only offer items that are currently in the
  slots** — this is AC4's gate.
- **Q5 → (b)** — a non-owned, non-exempt drop is blocked at the cap (a collection
  gate), and **there must be an SFX indicating it is not collectable** — this is
  AC8.
- **Q6 → (a)** — the choice gate follows the union: at full slots only items
  currently in the slots are offered (level-ups of permanent owned kinds, base
  picks for temp-held kinds, exempt entries).
- **Q7 → (a)** — exempt entries (`extra_life`, `mystery_ufo`) never occupy a slot;
  the flag exempts them from the count as well as from the spawn gate.

### Assumptions that stand unless contradicted

- A3 no HUD `N/6` readout; A4 the cap stays the named constant `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`;
  A5 the gyms obey the same rule; the permanent cannon and the `reset` utility never
  count; a repeat pickup of an already-slotted kind levels that slot and never adds a
  second one.
- Existing docs/tests asserting "field pickups never consume a slot" are **rewritten**,
  not deleted, once the decisions land.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 — plan skill: created 8 child items (4 test-first items before their implementation pairs, plus parity evidence and docs), wired 9 dependency edges, verified AC coverage, advanced stage to `plan_complete`. No existing content removed; producer answers Q1–Q3 and assumptions A3–A5 carried forward unchanged.
